_comment: U4's frontend half. A separate spec from u4_transcript_trim.json only because the spec
format carries one `command` and this one is vitest rather than pytest.
The frontend is where this feature can go wrong most quietly. Every mutation below leaves a
UI that renders, responds to clicks and reports success - the cut list just describes
something other than what the user struck out. Nothing throws, and the resulting clip looks
like a plausible edit, so only an assertion on the exact request body can tell.

mutations.name: cuts_never_merge
mutations.why: striking 'um uh' as two separate cuts removes the words and keeps the pause between them, which is the opposite of the intent - and doubles the filters in the render graph

mutations.name: cuts_merge_everything
mutations.why: merging non-adjacent selections cuts every word between them; the user loses speech they never struck

mutations.name: cut_uses_the_wrong_edge
mutations.old:
cuts.push({ start: words[runStart].start, end: words[runEnd].end });
  return cuts;
mutations.new:
cuts.push({ start: words[runStart].start, end: words[runEnd].start });
  return cuts;
mutations.why: ending the cut at the last word's START leaves that word in, so the final struck word of every run survives

mutations.name: out_of_range_indices_accepted
mutations.why: a selection held across a re-fetched, shorter transcript would index past the end and throw inside a click handler

mutations.name: cut_seconds_always_zero
mutations.old: return (cuts ?? []).reduce((total, cut) => total + Math.max(0, cut.end - cut.start), 0);
mutations.why: the previewed new length is the only feedback before a minute of CPU is spent; a wrong one is worse than none

mutations.name: api_drops_the_cuts
mutations.why: the request succeeds, the clip re-renders unchanged, and the user believes the edit was applied

mutations.name: api_hides_the_cuts_in_settings
mutations.why: the backend filters `settings` against known option fields and drops the rest silently - the exact failure the separate key exists to prevent

mutations.name: plain_rerender_leaks_the_click_event
mutations.why: React hands the handler its event, which would arrive where the cut list belongs; the request still validates as far as the client is concerned

mutations.name: selection_survives_a_clip_change
mutations.why: struck indices mean nothing against another clip's words, so a carried-over selection cuts arbitrary speech from the wrong clip

mutations.name: over_limit_submits_anyway
mutations.why: the backend answers 422 and the user gets a raw error instead of being stopped with the limit named

mutations.name: clear_does_not_clear
mutations.why: an edit that cannot be abandoned means the only way out of a mis-click is a page reload

mutations.name: editor_stays_open_after_applying
mutations.why: the clip record has been replaced, so the still-open editor shows a selection against word times that no longer describe the media - pressing apply again would cut the wrong thing

mutations.name: load_failure_reads_as_an_empty_transcript
mutations.old: error: error.message || "Could not load the transcript.",
mutations.why: 'no transcript available' and 'this clip has no speech' want opposite things from the user, and the API's own wording is what separates them
